text.p: Snyder Communications Inc soared almost 30 percent after its initial public offering, one of the hottest issues making market debuts on Wedneday.

Shares of Snyder, which provides outsourced marketing services, rose 4-5/8 to 21-5/8. It offered 7.8 million shares for $17 each, above its estimated pricing range of $14 to $16. The company cut terms of its IPO from 12 million shares. The offering was lead-managed by Merrill Lynch.
Other stocks which made their IPO market debuts today:

-- American Residential Services Inc ARS.N shares rose 2-1/4 to 17-1/4 in heavy trading. The company provides heating, ventilating and air conditioning systems (HVAC) services. The shares priced at $15, in the middle of their estimated pricing range.
-- Coffee People Inc shares slipped after their initial public offering. The stock slipped 3/4 from its IPO price of 9 to 8-1/4. It had been estimated to price in a range of $8.50 to $10.50.

-- LCC International Inc shares jumped about 23 percent, up 3-3/4 to 19-3/4. The Arlington, Virginia company provides radio frequency engineering and network design services for the wireless telecommunications industry. Its shares priced at $16, above its estimated range of $13 to $15.
-- Peerless Systems Inc, which develops software to control printer systems, also slipped after its IPO. The shares moved to 10-3/8 from its IPO price of $11.

-- Ocwen Financial Corp surged almost 33 percent after its initial public offering. The company offered 2.0 million shares, which priced at $15, above its IPO range of $11.50 to $13.50. Ocwen shares opened at 9 and rapidly climbed to 20-1/4, up 5-1/4.
Ocwen buys and resolves troubled loans. It had $1.9 billion of total assets at June 30, 1996.

-- Tri-Point Medical Corp stock was flat after its IPO, lead-managed by Lehman Brothers. Tri-Point offered three million shares, which priced at $8, below its estimated range of $10 to $12. The company makes adhesive products to close and seal wounds.
-- Shares of the Morgan Stanley Russia & New Europe Fund Inc slipped at their market debut, off 3/8 to 19-5/8. The closed-end fund offerred five million shares for $20 each.
Snyder led New York Stock Exchange stocks in terms of percent gains, and was one of the most heavily traded stocks on the NYSE.
